Subject: Latency contract experiment matrix and demo scripting

Jason — thanks again for carving out time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before engineering starts the POC run: 

Summary of ask (from your team):
- Verify end-to-end p95 and p99 latency for a mix of single-turn text generation and streaming responses at realistic traffic (QPS + bursts).
- Validate streaming concurrency behavior (many concurrent short streams per second).
- Confirm fallback behavior when the hosted fleet hits capacity (incumbent provider behavior is the baseline).

What Redwood will run for the POC (proposed):
1) Experiment matrix: small, medium, large traffic envelopes (see attached p95p99_experiment_matrix.xlsx). Each cell contains: qps, avg token length, concurrency target, percent streaming calls.
2) Traffic generator scripts: we’ll use the demo_script_streaming.sh (attached) to replay envelopes against both your current endpoint and a Redwood hosted canary.
3) Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn, p99 <= 900ms for streaming envelopes at the agreed medium envelope. If we miss, we’ll collect traces and isolate kernel/queueing contributions.

Decision points we need from Orbital before Wed 12 Aug:
- Final traffic envelope (attach a CSV with real hourly QPS if you can) — I attached orbital_traffic_envelope_v1.csv as a starter.
- Which endpoint we should validate as the “incumbent baseline” (please confirm full URL/credentials).
- Any procurement constraints on test keys or IP allowlists (cc procurement if needed).

Attachments: p95p99_experiment_matrix.xlsx, demo_script_streaming.sh, SLA-draft-Redwood-v1.docx, orbital_traffic_envelope_v1.csv

Next steps: we’ll schedule a 45m readout after the POC run with engineering, ops, and your staff to walk traces and decide SLA wording. Proposed windows: Aug 18–20 (we can lock once you confirm the baseline).

Thanks — I’ll stand up the matrix once we have the final envelope.

—
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Looping in our technical plan so Jason and ops have visibility. High level: we’ll run 3 staged experiments (non-concurrent baseline, steady-state concurrency, burst + tail probe). Details below.

Planned experiments (short):
- Stage A (baseline): 60s warmup at 0.5x medium envelope, collect end-to-end traces + kernel metrics.
- Stage B (steady concurrency): run 300s with N concurrent streaming clients (N from matrix) capturing p95/p99 across stream connect time and token-streaming time.
- Stage C (burst/tail): inject short bursts (3–5x QPS for 30s) and measure queuing/backpressure behavior and fallback to smaller model variant.

Important engineering asks for Orbital:
- Please provide a lightweight request example (headers + body) so we can match client RTT and tokenization. If you have a short prompt set representative of 70% of production calls, please share.
- Confirm TLS mutual auth or IP allowlist for the test key.

Artifacts we’ll push to the drive when runs are complete: raw latencies.csv, heap/profile traces, KV cache hit rates, and a summarized p95/p99 matrix.

I attached demo_script_streaming.sh — it uses wrk + a small Go harness that replays chunked responses. We’ll parameterize token lengths and inter-message gaps to simulate typing.

If everyone is OK, I’ll spin up the canary and coordinate a dry-run on Aug 16 (internal only) and then the joint window Aug 18.

—
Aditya Rao
Principal SRE (Inference), Redwood Inference

Two quick commercial/ops notes on the SLA wording and fallback behavior: 

1) SLA framing: procurement will want objective measurement and a single-point-of-truth artifact (we propose the summarized p95/p99 matrix in Drive as that artifact). Can we agree we’ll use the Redwood run summaries as the measurement for the POC? That avoids disagreements over sampling windows.

2) Fallback: for the POC we’ll demonstrate an automatic fallback to a quantized model variant under sustained queueing. Important to call out that fallback can change per-token quality; we should capture a small eval set pre/post fallback so product can assess quality delta.

3) Throughput guidance: for sizing capacity, please confirm your expected 99th percentile concurrency per user/session. If you don’t have that, we’ll default to the matrix’s concurrency column but prefer real numbers.

I’ll prepare a short redline to SLA-draft-Redwood-v1.docx and push to Drive; procurement can pull that before sending official redlines.

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
